articles.title: Plagiarism Allegations Force Former Cambridge Professor to Cancel Public Appearance
articles.summary: Jason Arday, who resigned as Cambridge's youngest Black professor amid plagiarism allegations, has canceled a September talk in London. He admitted early-career errors but said relentless scrutiny has taken a 'profound toll.' His memoir is still set for release.

articles.title: A Capital Under Guard: The $1.4 Billion Deployment Shaping D.C.’s Future
articles.summary: More than 4,600 National Guard troops have been patrolling Washington, D.C., for a year, and their mission just got extended to 2029 at a cost of $1.4 billion. Residents and leaders are pushing back, but the city’s unique status limits their power.

articles.title: In the Shadow of America’s Nuclear Past, a Startup Flips the Switch on a Truck-Sized Reactor
articles.summary: At Idaho National Laboratory, startup Deployable Energy achieved its first sustained chain reaction in a micro reactor — a pivotal moment for a new generation of portable nuclear power. But critics warn that safety oversight is being slashed.
